Source and eligibility
https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/bronze-sandcastle-deploys-modified-meterpreter-shells
The saved article.txt contains only a headline and summary. The full HTML and extracted text are preserved as article.html and page-text.txt beside this evidence.
The article explicitly reports vssadmin.exe shadow-copy creation before copying Windows ntds.dit. This named tool, exact database path component, and described acquisition mechanism provide the reconstructable artifact. Samples are synthetic behavior reconstructions, not recovered malware or verbatim commands. Their snapshot number (12), output filename, and language-specific copy API choices are illustrative. They assume snapshot 12 is the selected existing snapshot; they are static-analysis specimens and were not executed.

Extracted figures and code
All eleven figures were downloaded into images/ and inspected. There are no HTML pre/code blocks in the article body. Executable fragments in figures are recorded below. The two final figures are geographic/activity charts, not code.
Figure 1: aez.zip read by dllhost.exe; javaw.exe (clean), jli.dll (malicious), and config.ini (encrypted payload) under c:\programdata\microsoft\appv\.
Figure 2: mov edx,dword ptr ds:[r15+rax*4]; inc edx; bswap edx; lea ecx,qword ptr ds:[rax+rbx]; ror edx,cl; not edx; mov ecx,E7F122EB; sub ecx,eax; rol edx,cl; neg edx; rol edx,cl; movsxd rax,edx; jmp qword ptr ds:[rdi+rax*8]. Opcode sequence and fixed arithmetic constant are not promoted into family rules: no broader evidence that a byte fingerprint survives compiler/register changes.
Figure 3: decoded payload begins MZER with a reflective execution stub and embedded PE-like material; not sufficient to infer standard Metasploit ROR13 resolution (the article explicitly rules that out).
Figure 4: LoadLibraryA, kernel32.dll, ExceptionPOI.dll, winhttp.dll; BeaconDataParse, BeaconDataInt, BeaconDataShort, BeaconDataLength, BeaconDataExtract, BeaconFormatAlloc, BeaconFormatReset, BeaconFormatFree, BeaconFormatAppend, BeaconFormatPrintf, BeaconFormatToString, BeaconFormatInt, BeaconPrintf, BeaconOutput, BeaconUseToken, BeaconRevertToken, BeaconIsAdmin, BeaconGetSpawnTo. These shared Beacon-compatible interfaces do not uniquely identify COFFLoader or this family.
Figure 5: C++ decorated names include collect_screenshot@Client, collect_process@Client, collect_keylog@Client, listen_serv@Client, determine_keylogger_cmd@Client, determine_proxy_cmd@Client, determine_ablyProxy_cmd@Client. Names alone do not prove the implementation of data collection or an Ably command channel, so no generic collection/C2 convictions are added.
Figure 6: JSON top-level guid, info, type; info keys Domain, WindowsVersion, client_version, codePage, cpu_type, currentDirectory, customProxy, dhj_exe, execution_method, hostname, internalIP, is_needlock, last_sleep, listProcessNames, pid, processName, publicIP, start_time, username. Shown client_version=1.1.7 and type=serv. These telemetry fields are not sufficient for a malicious verdict alone.
Figure 7: GET /repos/LatonyCharnleyaW/Trix/contents/main.hr9c8qtx.js.map HTTP/1.1; Host: api.github.com; Content-Type and Accept: application/json; Authorization: token <redacted>; browser User-Agent and X-CSRF-TOKEN. No credentials are reconstructed or fetched. GitHub configuration retrieval alone remains neutral.
Figure 8: LatonyCharnleyaW profile, public Havo repository. No package release/version is identified.
Figure 9: README.md, abchannel.ts, channel.ts, kl.ts, moveDir.ts, pr.ts, scr.ts. Files are described as encrypted configurations/possible implants; .ts extensions do not establish npm packages. A displayed short Git commit is not a file hash.
Figures 10 and 11: victim distribution and working-hours heatmap; no additional IOCs.

Links followed
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sophoslabs/IoCs/master/BRONZESANDCASTLE_Meterpreter_IOCs.csv (saved iocs.csv)
https://github.com/trustedsec/COFFLoader and its raw README (saved coffloader-readme.txt). This is legitimate reference software, not a malicious package identity.

Indicators
SHA256 holds all 63 explicitly malicious file hashes from Sophos's linked IOC CSV: 21 SHA-256, 21 SHA-1 and 21 MD5. Original type/description relationships are retained in iocs.csv. No clean loader hashes were included in that list.
ENDPOINTS holds the eight article-reported hosts. dc.cathaypacifice.com and net.dpworldto.com are designated C2 servers. file.io, gofile.io, ably.net, ably.io, github.com, and api.github.com are legitimate shared services observed in this activity; their inclusion records this specific use, not malicious ownership. GitHub owner/repository/path context is preserved above. Do not block shared services by hostname alone.
PURLS is intentionally empty: no malicious versioned package coordinate is supplied. Implant versions 1.1.5/1.1.7 do not imply a distributable package or a source-package identity for Sandboxie, Java, Krita, NVDA, LINE, Sysinternals, or COFFLoader.

Detection and taxonomy review
Retained changed rules: micro-behaviors/fs/volume/shadow-copy/windows.yaml adds source-code scope for neutral VSS command/path observations; the copy-command description explicitly states its actual path-reference evidence.
objectives/credential-access/dump/output-file/shadow-copy.yaml broadens NTDS snapshot paths to escaped/repeated separators and source files, adds a source-argument-bound copy call observation, and allows that copy observation to satisfy the existing VSS credential-acquisition chain. Snapshot paths remain suspicious neutral filesystem observations; the complete VSS operation plus credential database copy chain remains hostile. Existing shared-service/network/crypto behavior has not been invented to obtain additional hostile counts.
All firing suspicious/hostile observations were checked: each sample contains an NTDS snapshot source path and vssadmin creation followed by a copy operation; C and Python additionally bind that path to copy argument zero. The batch and PowerShell source operands use the same actual device path. There is no Defender disablement, hive extraction, wiping, exfiltration, or Metasploit-specific identity assertion in these samples.
All four initial atomscan reports pass the suspicious floor (one hostile plus one or two suspicious findings). Samples are kept in suspicious/ because none is forced to meet the two-hostile floor by adding unsupported behavior. Atomscan's initial scan emitted complete local reports; its optional hopper upload returned HTTP 500 and did not affect local trait matching.
Permanent positive fixtures and benign controls are in this trait repository's testdata directories consumed by cleave validation. Ordinary user-file backups remain neutral; a snapshot NTDS path supplied only as a destination, or mentioned in a comment, may retain the existing path observation but must not activate the new source-copy observation or hostile acquisition chain.

Validation-driven placement correction
The first make validate run rejected the two benign path-only controls because their path-reference finding still lived in objectives/. A score cap cannot exempt an intent finding. Rather than weaken assertions or alter severity, that observation was relocated to micro-behaviors/fs/path/account-db::shadow-copy-ntds-database-path, keeping the broadened matcher, scope, suspicious severity, and confidence. Both controls now require the neutral-path finding and forbid source-copy and hostile-acquisition findings. Permanent positive expectations and the hostile acquisition composite reference the new exact ID.
Source inventory: shadow-copy-ntds-path moved to the filesystem path leaf; shadow-copy-registry-hive-path, shadow-copy-registry-hive-dump, defender-disabled-ntds-dump, shadow-copy-ntds-exfiltration, and shadow-copy-ntds-then-wipe remain in the original file; shadow-copy-ntds-dump remains with the documented new copy-call alternative. New shadow-copy-ntds-copy-call is an intentional coverage addition, not a placement-only change. The path matcher broadening and source-scope additions are likewise intentional coverage changes, tested separately from the ID relocation.
Ancestor-selector audit found five consumers: two MCP/config-injection rules in objectives/supply-chain/trojanized/app/config-injection/ide-mcp.yaml; Feishu and Slack rules in objectives/exfiltration/messaging/webhook/traits.yaml; and web-served-credential-loot-drop in objectives/exfiltration/http/webroot-drop/server-app.yaml. They require credential harvesting/theft evidence, so their objective directory selectors intentionally no longer admit a path-only reference. They continue to admit the credential source-copy observation and acquisition chain where their scopes allow them. No neutral-path fallback was added. Other original shadow-copy observations are retained with their references; none of these samples fires the registry-hive branches.
